title: CC-Test acceptance criteria, version 1
description: Vocabulary for declaring what a validation case must satisfy to be called PASS. Three families: 'bitwise' (whole-model run pairs - PyCAM5, freeCAM) is complete; 'unit-differential' (per-unit gates run by RecastEngine and summarised in a verification.json - clubb-jax, clm-ml-jax, elm-jax) is complete; 'statistical' (whole-model ensemble criteria) is provisional and must be finalised before any evidence is accepted against it. Every rule carries an explicit 'gating' flag: a check that is computed but does not gate must say so, so that the meaning of PASS is never implicit.

acceptance.description: The acceptance block of one validation case.

bitwiseAcceptance.description: Bit-for-bit agreement between a reference run and a candidate run.

rules.description: At least one rule must be gating; an acceptance block in which nothing gates cannot produce a meaningful PASS.

bitwiseRule.description: One bitwise check. The 'check' value selects the rule shape.

ruleFileSetEqual.description: The reference and candidate run directories must expose the same set of output files. A mismatch is an ERROR, not a FAIL: nothing was compared.

scope.description: Glob describing which outputs are in scope, e.g. '*.cam.{h0,r,rh0,rs}.*.nc'.

ruleNumericMd5Equal.description: Per output file, the md5 of a fixed-format text dump of all numeric variables must be identical between reference and candidate. Note this is one digest per file over the concatenated variable dump, not one digest per variable.

scope.description: Glob describing which output files this rule covers.

dump_format.description: Format string passed to 'ncks -s'. The digest is only comparable between manifests that used the same format, so it is recorded rather than assumed.

dump_tool.description: Tool that produced the dump. Recorded for the same reason as dump_format.

ruleCharDiffCount.description: Number of character variables whose per-variable dump digest differs. Character variables in CAM output routinely carry timestamps and case names, so this is normally reported without gating.

expect.description: Expected number of differing character variables.

ruleTimingDeltaPct.description: Relative wall-clock change per GPTL timer, as (candidate / reference - 1) * 100. Performance is reported alongside correctness but must not gate a correctness verdict unless a benchmark explicitly says otherwise.

timers.description: GPTL timer names, e.g. physpkg_st1, bc_physics, CPL:RUN_LOOP.

max_abs_pct.description: Optional bound on |delta_pct|. Only meaningful when gating is true.

unitDifferentialAcceptance.description: Per-unit differential gates, as RecastEngine runs them: every translated unit is compared against the compiled or recorded original and receives a verdict per verifier. The measurements this block reads come from the engine's run summary (`recast run ... --summary verification.json`, `schema: 1`): one entry per unit, one verdict per verifier, each verdict carrying a confidence and its metrics. The rules decide which of those recorded measurements gate; they never recompute anything. A unit that has no verdict from the named verifier is unevaluable, not passing.

summary_schema.description: The `schema` value of the RecastEngine summary these rules are written against. A summary with any other value is not read.

rules.description: At least one rule must be gating.

unitDifferentialRule.description: One per-unit check. The 'check' value selects the rule shape.

ruleUnitSetEqual.description: The summary must cover exactly these units - no fewer, no more. Always gating, for the same reason file_set_equal is: a PASS over a narrower unit set than the benchmark names is the cheapest path to green, and the one this rule closes. Units are named as the summary names them, e.g. 'fortran:advance_clubb_core_module'.

ungatedUnits.description: Units this rule does not judge, keyed by unit name as the summary spells it, each with the reason. They must still appear in the summary (unit_set_equal names them), so a reader sees that they exist and were not gated; the rule skips them and lists them in its detail. This is how a benchmark states a known coverage gap - a routine no recording reaches, an oracle that cannot be built - instead of leaving the unit out of the unit set, which would hide the gap.

ruleConfidenceAtLeast.description: Every unit's verdict from the named verifier must reach at least this rung of the engine's confidence ladder (weakest to strongest: sampled, toleranced, ulp_bounded, bit_exact, symbolic; 'failed' is below all of them). 'bit_exact' on 'differential.bitexact' is the NumPy translation gate; 'sampled' on 'static.rwset' is the dataflow gate.

verifier.description: Verifier name as the summary records it, e.g. 'differential.bitexact'.

ruleUlpTiered.description: The tiered ULP criterion for a target that cannot be bit-exact by construction (a JAX port under XLA): every dominant element - within dominant_at of its row's maximum - must be within ulp_gate ULP of the reference, and every element within rel_gate relative. Decision D4 as settled 2026-09-24 from what recast.verify.tolerance already enforces. The verifier records the gate it ran with (metrics ulp_gate, rel_gate); make_manifest.py requires those to equal the values here, so a benchmark and a run that describe different criteria cannot produce a PASS. A unit that is accepted beyond ulp_gate because of measured conditioning must be listed in waivers with its own bound and the reason - the waiver is written here, in the benchmark, never inferred from the verdict.

dominant_at.description: An element is dominant when it is within this fraction of its row's maximum magnitude, e.g. 1.0e-3. Declared here; checked against the verdict when the verifier records it.

waivers.description: Per-unit relaxation of ulp_gate, keyed by unit name as the summary spells it.

ruleNanMaskEqual.description: The candidate and the reference must be non-finite at exactly the same elements (metrics nan_mismatch == 0 for every unit). A fill value that moved is a real difference between the runs.

statisticalAcceptance.description: PROVISIONAL - pending decision D4 in docs/VALIDATION-ARCHITECTURE.md. Agreement within a stated tolerance or within ensemble spread, for cases where bit-for-bit reproduction is not the goal. The rule shapes below are placeholders derived from the Pipeline 2 dashboard figures (Held-Suarez 1.24e-6 relative difference; TJ2016 7.52e-3 within ensemble spread). Tolerance semantics, the norm, the compared variable set, and the spread test are NOT yet agreed. verify_evidence.py must reject 'statistical' acceptance until this block is marked final.

status.description: Must read 'provisional' while D4 is open. Removing this field is the signal that the vocabulary has been agreed.

ruleRelativeDiffMax.description: PROVISIONAL. Bound on the relative difference between reference and candidate fields.

variables.description: OPEN (D4): the compared variable set is not yet defined.

norm.description: OPEN (D4): which norm the tolerance applies to.

ruleWithinEnsembleSpread.description: PROVISIONAL. The candidate must fall within the spread of a reference ensemble.

members.description: OPEN (D4): required ensemble size is not yet agreed.

spread_metric.description: OPEN (D4): which spread definition counts as 'within'.

spread_multiplier.description: OPEN (D4): e.g. 2.0 for a two-sigma band.
